rules: Describe only what this test's assertions prove. Do not guess what the author intended.
The parser_facts are counted from the code and are correct. Use them.
Assertions can live in a helper the test calls. Read the helpers from the same file before you answer that a test asserts nothing.

facets.name: oracle
facets.goal: Say what the assertions of this test check. Choose the option that covers the strongest assertion in the test.

options.outcome: A result produced by running real product code: a return value, a response, stored state, a raised domain error, rendered output, a parsed or computed value.
options.boundary_effect: What the product sent to a system outside it, recorded by a fake of that outside system, with the content checked (a message, a request to a third party, an event and its properties). A test that only checks the outside system was called, or called once, is 'interaction'.
options.interaction: Only that a patched function, method or collaborator inside the same product was called, not called, or called with certain arguments. No result of real code is checked.
options.wording: That one source file, template, document or configuration file contains or lacks a string or pattern. The file is read as text and searched.
options.repo_rule: A rule that must hold across many files or modules, found by scanning or importing them: package boundaries, forbidden imports, every command is registered, two generated artefacts agree.
options.definition: That a constant, enum member, default value, field list, type or config key equals what its own definition says. The test restates a definition and runs no logic.
options.no_error: A validator or guard function is called with a specific, deliberately built input, and the test passes when it raises nothing. Use this only when raising or not raising is that function's whole output. A test that calls code and checks nothing is 'nothing'.
options.nothing: Nothing meaningful: no assertion in the test or its helpers, or only that a value exists or has a type.

facets.name: subject
facets.goal: Say what kind of thing this test exercises.

options.public_behaviour: Behaviour a user, API client, operator or another module can observe: a command, a service or domain function, a handler, permission rules, a parser or calculation with real inputs.
options.internal_detail: A private helper, an internal step, internal call order, log wording, or internal data layout that could change in a refactor with no behaviour change.
options.repo_tooling: Repository tooling and not the product: CI workflows and their scripts, lint rules, agent configuration, hooks, developer scripts, documentation.
options.test_support: Test fixtures, fakes, test harness or evaluation tooling.

facets.name: real_code
facets.goal: Say where the values the test asserts on come from.

options.real: From real product code. Mocks, if any, stand in only for things outside the product (network, clock, file system of another program, third-party service).
options.partly_mocked: From real product code, but some collaborators inside the product are patched, so a thinner slice of the product runs.
options.from_mocks: Mostly from values the test configured its own mocks or fakes to return.
options.no_code_run: No product code runs; the values come from reading files or constants.

facets.name: risk_area
facets.goal: Say whether the thing this test checks is itself an access, money or data-loss rule.

options.protected: The rule the test checks is itself about access, money, security or not losing data.
